key_insight: VATC combines declared agent traffic, router-side verification, and rate-limited priority service to reduce agent queuing delay while protecting human traffic from spoofed floods.
engineering_relevance: Network engineers could use VATC to manage agent-heavy congestion, but its value depends on classifier robustness and queue-rate tuning.
method: Mark agent flows with a reserved DSCP value.
Demote flows that contradict their agent declaration to below best-effort service.
Serve accepted agent traffic through a rate-limited priority queue.
evidence_signal: Across two simulators and a Linux kernel, VATC cut mean agent queuing delay 98% versus DiffServ in a simulated burst with immediate verification, raised human delay 12%, and kept human latency 11× lower under a kernel-tested spoofed flood.
watch_item: Verification remains fragile: the classifier missed six agent-mimicking spoofers, and emulated network delay erased a timing feature’s ability to distinguish agent from human flows.
paper_title: Verifiable Agentic Traffic Class: A Policed Quality-of-Service Mechanism for Agentic AI Traffic, Evaluated from Simulation to Real-Kernel Adversarial Testing
